title: Coaxial TSV whose liner doubles as on-die decoupling capacitor
idea: Combine the HBM power TSV with a deep-trench MIM capacitor: build each power via as a coaxial stack (Cu core / ZrO2-Al2O3 high-k liner / doped-Si or TiN outer shell) so the ~50 um via sidewall supplies roughly 5-10 pF of decap. Thousands of power TSVs then become the stack's decoupling bank and the periphery's planar MOS decap arrays are deleted.
why: Periphery (~49% of die) and HBM TSV keep-out tax: reclaims ~3-6% die area and lowers PDN noise so VDDQ margin and I/O energy drop ~5-10%; keep-out zones do double duty.

title: Interposer fabbed as a mature-node DRAM capacity tier
idea: Combine the passive silicon interposer (2,500+ mm2 of idle silicon under every AI package) with a 2x-nm-class trench-capacitor DRAM array built into the same wafer in depreciated 300 mm lines, wired to the GPU by mm-scale interposer traces as a near tier between HBM and CXL. Arrays are tiled with stitched redundancy so a bad block is fused off instead of scrapping the interposer.
why: Capacity and capital intensity: ~10-30 GB extra per package at mature-node cost/bit with zero added footprint and ~2-4 pJ/bit access; shifts bits off scarce EUV-node wafers.

title: Light-through-silicon vias: 1310 nm optical bus vertically through stack
idea: Combine silicon's transparency at 1310 nm with HBM die stacking: keep small metal-free windows in each ~30 um thinned die and place a wavelength-selective vertical grating coupler plus ring modulator/Ge detector at each window, so a single WDM beam injected from the base die rises through all 12-16 dies and each die drops/adds its own wavelength. Photons replace most data TSVs.
why: HBM TSV tax (~3x area/bit, 20-30% yield loss): replacing 1,000+ data TSVs with a few optical windows cuts stacking area overhead and TSV-related yield loss, enabling >16-high stacks.

title: Copper-free capacitive hybrid bond: dielectric bond doubles as signal coupler
idea: Combine oxide-oxide direct bonding with AC-coupled proximity signaling: each die-to-die signal is two overlapping metal plates separated only by the ~0.5 um bond oxide, driven with edge/pulse signaling, so no Cu pads must touch. Only a sparse grid of coarse TSVs carries DC power.
why: HBM stacking yield and alignment: removes Cu dishing/protrusion defects and tightens nothing beyond plate overlap (~+/-1 um) at 2-3 um signal pitch; <0.05 pJ/bit per hop; claims to recover most of the 20-30% stack yield loss.

title: Sense-amplifier row latch reconfigured as on-die serializer
idea: Combine the bitline sense-amp row (an 8-16 kb latch already holding the opened page) with a SerDes shift register: add a segment-level pass chain so the latched row shifts directly into a local high-speed serializer next to the mat, bypassing column decoders, global I/O lines and the central datapath for streaming reads.
why: Overfetch and periphery: for streaming AI weight reads the 'overfetched' 128x row is actually used; cuts internal data-movement energy ~30-50% and column/global-I/O periphery area.

title: Coolant that is also the power supply: in-stack redox microchannels
idea: Combine interlayer microfluidic cooling with a redox flow battery: a vanadium or organic electrolyte pumped through microchannels between HBM dies passes porous electrodes on each die, generating ~1 V locally while carrying away heat, so most power TSVs and bumps are replaced by fluid.
why: HBM TSV tax and thermal ceiling: power/ground TSVs are roughly half the via count; replacing them frees ~30-50% of TSVs and lets stacks grow past today's thermal limit.

title: DRAM dies embedded in glass-core substrate cavities under processor
idea: Combine the glass-core package substrates now arriving for AI packages with embedded-die technology: laser-form cavities in the glass core, embed thinned commodity DRAM/LPDDR dies face-up, and connect them with through-glass vias straight up into the GPU bump field so memory sits ~300 um below compute instead of beside it.
why: Data movement and CoWoS/HBM bottleneck: ~1-2 pJ/bit vertical links vs 3-4 pJ/bit HBM, no silicon interposer, no TSV stack (avoids 3x HBM area tax), uses commodity DRAM wafers.

title: Backscatter chiplet links: memory dies reflect a shared mm-wave carrier
idea: Combine RFID backscatter with in-package interconnect: the host radiates one 60-300 GHz carrier into a shielded package cavity and each memory die switches the impedance of a small on-die antenna to reflect its data; memory dies need no oscillator, PA or bump field for data.
why: Data-movement energy and assembly: transmit energy at the memory die ~0.1 pJ/bit; dies can sit unbonded/swappable in the cavity, removing TSV/bond yield loss for capacity tiers.

title: Voltage-stacked HBM: dies wired in series to recycle supply current
idea: Combine voltage stacking (charge recycling) with die stacking: power a 12-high HBM from ~12 V with each die in its own 1 V domain in series, small on-die push-pull regulators balancing mismatch and level-shifting signal TSVs crossing domains. The same current is reused by every die.
why: PDN and TSV tax: supply current falls ~12x, cutting power TSV/bump count (about half of all TSVs) and IR drop; ~5-10% die area recovered and interposer PDN losses reduced.

title: One modulated laser beam powers and clocks the stack's top die
idea: Combine power-over-fiber photovoltaics with optical clock distribution: a modulated 1550 nm laser lands on InGaAs photovoltaic cells bonded to the top HBM die; the DC part powers the top die's I/O and refresh logic and the envelope yields a low-jitter clock redistributed downward, deleting clock TSVs and per-die DLLs.
why: Clock/DLL power (~10-15% of DRAM I/O power) and skew in tall stacks: enables >20-high stacks without clock TSVs and trims PDN TSV count.

title: Address-event memory bus transmits only nonzero values as spikes
idea: Combine neuromorphic address-event representation with the DRAM interface: the base die encodes each burst as (index, value) events for nonzero bytes and drives an asynchronous clockless bus that toggles only when an event fires; zero runs cost no transitions and the host rebuilds dense lines.
why: Interface energy and effective bandwidth: quantized ML activations/KV caches are 40-90% zero; 2-5x lower interface energy and higher effective bandwidth on sparse tensors.

title: DRAM bonded onto processor backside, sharing its backside power network
idea: Combine backside power delivery (BSPDN, arriving at 2 nm logic) with memory stacking: hybrid-bond a thinned DRAM die onto the logic die's backside PDN layer and reuse the same nano-TSV process that brings power in to carry memory signals, keeping the front side for signals and cooling.
why: Data movement: ~0.2-0.5 pJ/bit vs 3-4 pJ/bit HBM, no interposer, no HBM base die, reuses backside steps already paid for in logic fabs.

title: Array-only DRAM wafers bonded to one shared logic periphery tier
idea: Combine CMOS-bonded-array (Xtacking-style 3D NAND) with multi-tier DRAM: fabricate array-only wafers with no sense amps or decoders, then bond 2-4 of them through vertical bitline/wordline vias at ~2 um hybrid-bond pitch onto a single advanced-logic wafer carrying all sense amps, decoders and I/O.
why: Periphery (~49% of die) and masks: array wafers need fewer masks and cheap transistors while periphery gets fast logic; claims 30-45% lower cost/bit and 1.6-2x bits per footprint.

title: Active interposer merging HBM base dies with GPU memory controllers
idea: Combine the HBM logic base die and the GPU-side memory controller/PHY into one active interposer in a 12-16 nm logic node: DRAM core stacks bond directly onto it with controllers right underneath, so both ends of the PHY pair vanish and the GPU reaches memory over on-chip-style wires.
why: Data movement and GPU beachfront: removes ~1-1.5 pJ/bit of the 3-4 pJ/bit HBM cost and ~10% of GPU die area spent on PHYs/controllers.

title: One end-to-end code spanning DRAM array ECC and link FEC
idea: Combine on-die ECC with the interface's link CRC/FEC: compute one strong RS/LDPC code over the line plus metadata at write time, store its parity in the array, and transmit stored parity over the link unchanged so the host corrects array and channel errors in a single decode.
why: Periphery and I/O energy: deletes on-die ECC logic (~3-5% die area) and duplicate link ECC; tolerating link BER ~1e-6 permits lower swing for ~20-30% I/O energy savings.

title: Resonant adiabatic memory bus recycles wire charge via LC tank
idea: Combine resonant clocking's on-chip LC tank with the wide data bus: interposer/HBM data lines become part of a resonant network where transitioning lines swing sinusoidally through an inductor and hand their CV2 energy back to the tank instead of dumping it to ground; steady bits park.
why: Data movement and the voltage floor: recovers ~50-70% of bus switching energy at interposer lengths without lowering voltage.

title: VCSEL arrays on HBM top die, fibers routed inside cold plate
idea: Combine the liquid cold plate already sitting on HBM stacks with optical I/O: bond VCSEL and photodiode arrays on the top core die (fed by TSVs from the base) and embed glass waveguide bundles inside the cold plate so light exits vertically through the plate to rack-scale memory or peer GPUs.
why: Package beachfront and pooling: adds Tb/s per stack from the top surface at ~1-2 pJ/bit over meters without consuming interposer edge.

title: Double-sided interposer with HBM mounted directly beneath the GPU
idea: Combine double-sided module assembly with 2.5D packaging: mount HBM stacks on the underside of a thin interposer directly under the GPU, connected by ~100 um through-interposer vias instead of 5-10 mm lateral wires, with the package substrate cavity-milled to receive them.
why: Data movement and interposer area: 50x shorter links (~0.5 pJ/bit), 8+ stacks without beachfront limits, ~40% smaller interposer.

title: Contactless inductive wafer probing at full speed for known-good dies
idea: Combine inductive-coupling transceivers with wafer sort: every DRAM core die carries a small coil-array test port so the prober couples wirelessly at full 6-10 Gb/s and runs retention, row-hammer and speed screens before thinning and stacking, with no probe damage or large test pads.
why: HBM yield (down 20-30%): stacking only truly known-good dies could recover about half that loss and remove test-pad area.

title: Base-die line compressor storing size tags in spare ECC bits
idea: Combine the HBM base die with a hardware cache-line compressor (base-delta plus shared FP8/BF16 exponents) whose per-line size tag lives in spare ECC/metadata bits, so two compressed lines pack into one slot transparently and the host sees normal addresses.
why: Doing DRAM's job with less: 1.3-2x effective capacity and bandwidth on AI tensors with no host software change.

title: Magnetically aligned nanowire underfill replacing microbumps
idea: Combine anisotropic conductive film with magnetic-field assembly: Ni-cored, Au-shelled nanowires dispersed in a curable underfill chain into vertical columns between pads under a field applied during bonding, then cure, giving 2-5 um pitch z-axis interconnect with no microbump plating or Cu CMP.
why: HBM stacking cost and warpage tolerance: claims 30-50% lower stacking cost and reworkable joints.

title: Open-standard base die enabling multi-vendor DRAM stacks
idea: Combine a royalty-free, open-source HBM base-die design (released like RISC-V) with a U.S. OSAT stacking line that buys known-good DRAM core wafers from any maker, including smaller and second-source DRAM fabs, so stacks can be assembled without the big three's TSV lines.
why: Usable supply and U.S. manufacturability: decouples HBM stacking capacity from three vendors, raising supply and creating domestic stacking capacity.

title: Wafer-scale processor bonded face-to-face to a whole DRAM wafer
idea: Combine wafer-scale compute (one 300 mm logic wafer) with wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding of an entire undiced DRAM wafer on top; defect-tolerant routing maps out bad DRAM tiles the same way wafer-scale engines map out bad cores. No dicing, TSV stacks or package.
why: Data movement and HBM tax: on the order of ~1 TB of DRAM directly above compute at <0.1 pJ/bit per bond hop, ~30x bandwidth density vs HBM.

title: MacEtch TSVs whose catalyst becomes the plating seed
idea: Combine metal-assisted chemical etching with via metallization: a perforated Au/Ag catalyst film sinks into silicon in HF/H2O2 at room temperature, carving 50-100 um vertical holes, and the same catalyst left at the via bottom serves as the seed for bottom-up Cu electroplating after an electrografted polymer liner. No Bosch DRIE (helium backside cooling) and no argon-sputtered seed.
why: TSV cost and rare-gas exposure: removes both rare-gas-dependent TSV steps and a costly plasma tool; claims 40-60% lower TSV module cost on U.S.-friendly wet benches.

title: Final CMP step doubles as bond activation, no plasma
idea: Combine CMP with surface activation: a tailored final-polish slurry (colloidal silica plus OH/amine terminating chemistry) leaves the SiCN or oxide bond face densely silanol-terminated and particle-free, and dies bond in-line within minutes, skipping the argon/N2 plasma activation chamber.
why: Hybrid-bond cost and rare-gas independence: removes a tool and queue-time limit, ~15-25% lower hybrid-bond module cost, enabling argon-free die-to-wafer HBM stacking.

title: Build the stack top-down on its own SiC heat spreader
idea: Combine the temporary thinning carrier with the final lid: bond the top core-die wafer face-down onto a permanent SiC wafer, thin it, then bond each next wafer face-down onto the previous backside, finishing with the base logic wafer, so the SiC wafer is the carrier for every step and becomes the heat spreader. No temporary bond/debond cycles and no excimer debond lasers (Xe/Kr in neon buffer).
why: Stacking cost, yield and thermal: eliminates N bond/debond cycles per stack and their yield loss, ~2x better top-side heat path (SiC ~370 W/mK), fully rare-gas-free.

title: On-die moisture sensor replaces helium leak testing of cavity packages
idea: Combine package sealing with an on-die interdigitated capacitive moisture sensor and micro-heater read out through DRAM test-mode registers: after sealing optical/mm-wave cavity memory packages, a short heat-soak and capacitance trend gives each unit's leak rate, and the sensor keeps monitoring in the field.
why: Rare-gas dependence of packaging QA: removes helium leak detection for cavity and photonic memory packages and adds field reliability telemetry at ~zero area.

title: Diode-laser photoreduction writes copper redistribution lines directly
idea: Combine laser direct imaging with metal deposition: coat a copper-formate/amine complex film, scan a 405 nm GaN diode-laser array to photothermally reduce it into 2-5 um Cu lines, rinse unexposed film and electroless-thicken. No photoresist, no excimer scanner (ArF/KrF need neon) and no argon-sputtered seed.
why: Capital and rare-gas intensity of RDL: maskless one-step RDL layers at ~50% lower cost using commodity GaN lasers, fully U.S. manufacturable.

title: Single LED-cured nanoimprint defines via and trench for interposers
idea: Combine nanoimprint lithography with dual damascene: a two-tier stamp imprints via and trench together into a UV-curable dielectric cured by 365 nm LED arrays, followed by electroless seed and Cu plating. No scanner, no excimer laser, no argon PVD.
why: Interposer capital and neon exposure: 0.5-1 um L/S interconnect without DUV, halving lithography steps per metal level.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory vault: 77 K DRAM pool with near-zero refresh
idea: Combine rack-scale CXL memory pooling with liquid-nitrogen immersion (N2 is 78% of air, unlike helium cryogenics): at 77 K access-transistor leakage collapses so retention stretches to hours, refresh nearly stops, wires are ~6-7x less resistive and commodity DRAM runs at reduced VDD.
why: Refresh (16-33% idle power, 10-20% bandwidth) goes to ~0 and racks pack 2-3x denser; net win for idle-heavy capacity tiers after ~10 W/W cryo-lift overhead.

title: Formic-acid vapor oxide reduction built into the Cu-Cu bonder
idea: Combine the solder industry's formic-acid oxide reduction with Cu-Cu micro-pillar thermocompression: dies and wafer are exposed to formic-acid vapor in nitrogen at ~200 C inside the bonder, reducing Cu2O, then pressed immediately in the same oxygen-free atmosphere, replacing argon plasma cleaning.
why: Rare-gas-free fine-pitch bonding at lower thermal budget (DRAM retention degrades with hot anneals); enables 3-10 um Cu-Cu memory stacking without argon.

title: Electroplated copper-manganese alloy that grows its own barrier
idea: Combine TSV electroplating with barrier formation: plate Cu-0.5%Mn from a non-aqueous or ionic-liquid bath onto an electroless seed; a 350 C anneal drives Mn to the oxide liner forming a few-nm MnSiO3 barrier and leaves pure Cu, deleting the argon-sputtered Ta/TaN barrier.
why: TSV cost and HBM area tax: removes a rare-gas PVD tool and enables thinner, higher-aspect TSVs with smaller keep-out zones.

title: Thermomigrated aluminum trails form TSVs with no etching
idea: Combine solar-cell thermal-gradient zone melting with through-silicon vias: print Al dots on an n-type wafer and apply a vertical temperature gradient (IR heating below, chilled plate above) so molten Al-Si droplets migrate through the wafer, leaving Al-saturated p+ columns (~1-2 ohm each) junction-isolated from the bulk.
why: TSV capital: no DRIE (helium cooling), no liner/barrier/seed PVD (argon), no plating; claims 5-10x cheaper vias for power/ground and slow signals.

title: Anodized aluminum oxide film as litho-free vertical interconnect interposer
idea: Combine cookware-style anodization with z-axis interconnect: anodize a 50-100 um aluminum sheet into a rigid self-ordered nanopore template (~10^9 pores/cm2), electroplate Cu into every pore and polish both faces, giving a ceramic film that conducts only vertically and connects any pad above to the pad below with no lithography or plasma.
why: Interposer capital and alignment: wet-only, rare-gas-free memory-on-logic interposer, pitch-agnostic so placement tolerance relaxes; ~10x cheaper than TSV interposers.

title: Drawn metal-cored glass preform sliced into via-dense interposers
idea: Combine optical-fiber preform drawing with interposer making: stack thousands of metal-cored glass rods into a preform (Taylor-wire process), draw it down until cores reach 5-10 um pitch, fuse into a boule and slice/polish it into wafers, each a through-glass-via interposer with millions of vias; the draw tower cools with N2/forced air rather than helium.
why: Interposer bottleneck and capital: no drilling, lithography or plasma; many interposers per draw from a ~$few-M tower; claims 5-10x cheaper vertical interconnect.

title: E-beam-personalized interposer routes around each stack's bad channels
idea: Combine post-stack HBM test maps with direct-write multi-beam e-beam lithography (vacuum only, no laser gas): after each stack is tested, one custom top routing layer is written per interposer that maps out defective channels/TSV lanes and wires in spares, so partially failing stacks ship at full capacity.
why: HBM yield (down 20-30%): recovering about half adds ~10-15% usable supply with no new DRAM wafers and no neon.

title: Chip-first printed fan-out: interconnect printed directly onto placed dies
idea: Combine pick-and-place die embedding with aerosol-jet printing: DRAM and controller dies sit face-up in a molded panel and Ag/Cu nanoparticle inks plus polyimide dielectric are printed across die edges at 10-20 um lines, then sintered with near-IR diode lasers instead of xenon flash lamps.
why: Packaging capex and rare-gas exposure: zero masks, vacuum or rare gas; 3-5x lower capex for LPDDR/CXL memory modules on U.S. soil.

title: Liquid-metal microchannel interconnects for reworkable memory-on-logic stacks
idea: Combine microfluidic channels with interconnect: a thin glass spacer with fiber-laser-drilled holes filled with gallium-indium eutectic sits between electroless Ni-P/Au barrier pads on memory and logic, so joints form at room temperature without plasma or bonding gases and a memory die can be removed and replaced.
why: Stacking yield and lifetime: rework recovers nearly all stacking yield loss and makes memory field-upgradable; rare-gas-free assembly.

title: Solution-grown YBCO superconducting interposer lines cooled by liquid nitrogen
idea: Combine coated-conductor chemistry (TFA-MOD chemical solution deposition of YBCO on solution-deposited buffers, no argon ion-beam assist or sputtering) with interposer wiring operated in LN2, so memory-to-processor transmission lines have zero DC resistance and carry low-swing signals over 10-50 cm without repeaters; no helium cryogenics.
why: Data movement and beachfront: ~0.1 pJ/bit over long reach decouples memory capacity from package edge length.

title: LED-lithography coarse wiring paired with ultra-wide slow low-swing bus
idea: Combine 365 nm UV-LED array exposure (solid-state: no Hg-Ar/Xe lamp, no neon excimer), which only patterns ~2-5 um lines, with an interface designed for that limit: 8-16k parallel interposer wires at 0.5-1 Gb/s, 100-150 mV swing, no SerDes or DLL, delivering TB/s from coarse wiring.
why: Data movement and capital: ~0.3-0.5 pJ/bit vs 3-4 pJ/bit HBM, with interposers made in PCB-class fabs; the constraint becomes the design driver.

title: Retired-server DRAM harvesting line feeding CXL expander cards
idea: Combine e-waste DIMM recovery with CXL memory expansion: an automated line desolders DDR4/DDR5 packages from retired DIMMs, reballs and characterizes each chip for retention and speed, bins them, and remounts them on CXL Type-3 cards whose controller maps weak rows and applies per-chip adaptive refresh. No new wafers, so no new rare gas.
why: Usable supply: millions of retired DIMMs per year become capacity at ~10-20% of new cost/bit during the shortage.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling replaces helium in TSV plasma etch
idea: Combine the electrostatic chuck's backside gas cooling with hydrogen, whose thermal conductivity (~0.18 W/m-K) beats helium's (~0.15), using a low-leak sealed chuck with H2 sensing and interlocks so TSV DRIE and other plasma steps keep wafer temperature control with no helium; H2 is made domestically by electrolysis.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline): keeps HBM TSV etch lines running independent of helium supply.

title: Gasless copper self-sputtering seeds high-aspect TSVs without argon
idea: Combine HiPIMS with sustained self-sputtering: above a threshold target power density ionized Cu atoms sustain the discharge on their own, so after brief ignition with N2 or H2 the process runs on copper vapor only, and the highly ionized flux is steered by substrate bias deep into 10:1 TSVs for conformal seeds.
why: Argon removal plus better step coverage: narrower TSVs and smaller keep-out zones shrink the HBM area tax.

title: Printed polymer optical waveguides replace helium-drawn glass fiber links
idea: Combine package build-up layers with optics: photo-pattern siloxane polymer waveguides (LED-cured) into the substrate and board to link co-packaged optical engines on GPUs and memory modules over 10-50 cm. Glass fiber needs helium for preform consolidation and draw cooling; polymer waveguides need none.
why: Optical memory disaggregation at ~1-2 pJ/bit without fiber-attach cost/yield, on a rare-gas-free supply chain.

title: Plastic dielectric waveguide carries sub-THz memory links between boards
idea: Combine CMOS 140-300 GHz transceivers with low-loss PTFE/HDPE dielectric ribbon waveguides plugged at the package edge, so memory boards reach compute over 0.5-2 m at 50-100 Gb/s per lane with no lasers, no glass fiber (helium-drawn) and no fine-pitch copper.
why: Data movement and pooling cost: ~1-2 pJ/bit, cheaper than optics and longer reach than copper, fully rare-gas-free.

title: Rare-gas content ledger in packaging PDKs and CHIPS grants
idea: Combine the packaging process-design kit with a per-step bill of gases: each OSAT/fab step declares its He/Ne/Ar/Kr/Xe consumption, EDA flows total it per product, and CHIPS-style packaging grants pay a per-stack bonus for products built on rare-gas-free flows.
why: Scarce-resource intensity and resilience: makes rare-gas exposure visible and pays for substitution across U.S. memory packaging, hedging Qatar-type outages.
